outputs.root_cause: In checkout/coupons.py, apply_coupons uses a mutable default argument `coupons: list[float] = []`. Python evaluates this default once at function definition, so the same list object is shared across all calls. Each call appends the customer's new_coupons into that shared list and never clears it, so coupons from earlier checkouts in the same process are applied to later carts. Restarting the process recreates the default list, which matches the report.

outputs.root_cause: Money.ToCents calls Math.Round(amount, 2) without a MidpointRounding argument, so it uses the default banker's rounding (ToEven). Exact half-cent values such as 2.345 round to the even neighbour 2.34, violating finance policy FIN-12, which requires halves to be rounded away from zero.

claims.claim: H1 supported: Money.cs rounds with Math.Round using the default MidpointRounding.ToEven (banker's rounding) instead of AwayFromZero, so exact half-cent values like 2.345 round to the even neighbour 2.34 when the preceding digit is even. The v3.0 change likely dropped an explicit MidpointRounding argument or changed the rounding call.
